questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Parliamentary System of Government' refers to.
questions.a: A parliamentary system of government is one in which the executive is drawn from and is responsible to the legislature, and the head of government is the leader of the majority party in parliament.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Parliamentary System of Government'.
questions.a: In a parliamentary system, the executive is collectively responsible to the legislature, ensuring continuous accountability.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Parliamentary System of Government' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Parliamentary System of Government

concepts.title: Parliament of India: Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Parliament of India: Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha' refers to.
questions.a: The Parliament of India consists of the President, the Lok Sabha (House of the People) and the Rajya Sabha (Council of States); together they form the union legislature.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Parliament of India: Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha'.
questions.a: The Lok Sabha is the directly elected lower house, while the Rajya Sabha is the indirectly elected upper house representing the states.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Parliament of India: Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Parliament of India

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Law-Making Process' refers to.
questions.a: The law-making process is the procedure by which a bill passes through three readings in each house of Parliament, receives the President's assent, and becomes an Act.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Law-Making Process'.
questions.a: A bill must pass both houses in identical form and receive the President's assent before it becomes law.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Law-Making Process' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Law-Making Process

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'President of India and Role' refers to.
questions.a: The President of India is the constitutional head of the state, elected by an electoral college, who exercises executive powers on the advice of the Council of Ministers.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'President of India and Role'.
questions.a: The President is the nominal head of the executive, while real executive power lies with the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.

questions.q: Under which section is 'President of India and Role' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: President of India

concepts.title: Prime Minister and Council of Ministers

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Prime Minister and Council of Ministers' refers to.
questions.a: The Prime Minister is the head of government and the leader of the Council of Ministers, which is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Prime Minister and Council of Ministers'.
questions.a: The Prime Minister is appointed by the President and selects the Council of Ministers, which holds the real executive power.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Prime Minister and Council of Ministers' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Prime Minister and Council of Ministers

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Parliamentary vs Presidential Democracy' refers to.
questions.a: In a parliamentary democracy the executive is drawn from and responsible to the legislature, whereas in a presidential democracy the executive is elected separately and is not responsible to the legislature.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Parliamentary vs Presidential Democracy'.
questions.a: The key difference lies in the relationship between the executive and the legislature: fused and responsible in parliamentary, separate and fixed-term in presidential.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Parliamentary vs Presidential Democracy' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Parliamentary vs Presidential Democracy

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Parliamentary Procedures' refers to.
questions.a: Parliamentary procedures are the rules and practices that govern the conduct of business in Parliament, including question hour, zero hour, debates, motions, and committees.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Parliamentary Procedures'.
questions.a: Parliamentary procedures such as question hour and motions allow members to scrutinise the government and hold it accountable.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Parliamentary Procedures' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Parliamentary Procedures

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Accountability of the Executive' refers to.
questions.a: Accountability of the executive is the principle that the Council of Ministers remains in office only as long as it enjoys the confidence of the Lok Sabha and must answer to Parliament for its actions.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Accountability of the Executive'.
questions.a: Through questions, motions, debates, and the no-confidence motion, Parliament ensures the executive is accountable to the people's representatives.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Accountability of the Executive' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Accountability of the Executive

questions.a: 543 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Composition of Parliament: Seats Calculation' refers to.
questions.a: The strength of a house of Parliament is the sum of seats allocated to states and union territories; the Lok Sabha currently has 543 elected members.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Composition of Parliament: Seats Calculation'.
questions.a: The total membership of a house is found by adding the seats from states and union territories.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Composition of Parliament: Seats Calculation', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: total_members = state_seats + union_territory_seats
